transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because I just can't stop focusing on my face. There's this... this rough, sunken-looking patch on it. Every time I pass a mirror or see a picture of myself, it's all I can see. It makes one side of me look real old and just beat-up. It bothers me a lot, honestly, even though people around me keep telling me they barely notice anything at all. But I know what I'm looking at, and I just can't stop seeing it.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or self-conscious in social situations, especially because of how you look?

Yeah, I do. It gets pretty bad right before I have to be around people. Like, before I head out to work, or if I'm supposed to go over to my sister’s for game night... I'll just end up stuck checking the bathroom mirror. I stand there turning my face, trying to see how it looks under different lights, and I catch myself just rubbing and rubbing at the spot. 

If I think it looks too obvious that day, I'll wear a hat pulled down real low to try and hide it. Or sometimes... I just make up an excuse not to go at all. It just makes me too self-conscious to sit there knowing people might be staring at it.
How much time would you say you spend each day thinking about that patch on your face or checking how it looks?

I don't really know exactly. I've never, you know, timed it with a watch or anything. But it feels like a lot. 

I mean, in the morning it's a good chunk of time right there at the bathroom sink. And then during the day... I work construction, so I'm busy, but it's always just kind of sitting there in the back of my mind. If I walk past a truck mirror on the site or go use the washroom, I'm stopping to look at it again. 

So... yeah, I couldn't give you an exact number of hours or anything like that, but it's definitely on my mind off and on all day long.
Does this concern about the patch on your face ever make it hard for you to focus at work, or cause you a lot of emotional distress even when you're not looking at mirrors?

I guess it does, yeah. I mean, at work, I'm supposed to be paying attention to what I'm doing—running equipment, moving materials—but sometimes I just zone out thinking about it. Like, I'll be wondering if the guys can see it when the sun hits my face a certain way. 

And as far as the distress goes... yeah, it bothers me a lot. Even if I'm just sitting at home watching TV, not looking in a mirror at all, I can still feel it there. It just makes me feel... I don't know, frustrated and down. It's just hard to turn it off.
Have you ever avoided doing certain things or stopped yourself from going places because of how you feel about that patch on your face, even if it wasn’t a social situation?

Yeah, I have. Like I mentioned earlier about skipping out on game night at my sister's... but it's not just social stuff. It messes with work, too. 

There have been mornings where I'm actually late getting out the door for a job because I get stuck in the bathroom checking it. And on the site, if the foreman or somebody is taking progress photos or group shots, I always dodge them. I'll just walk the other way or pretend I need to go grab a tool. I just really don't want people looking at my face, let alone having it caught in a picture.
Do you think about the patch on your face as a defect or flaw in your appearance, and do you believe it makes you look ugly or unattractive?

Yeah, I definitely see it as a flaw. That's really the whole reason I'm here. I just can't stop seeing this... this rough, sunken-looking patch on my face. Every time I look in the mirror or see a photo, it's right there. It makes one side of my face look all old and beat-up. It makes me feel ugly, yeah. And the frustrating part is, when I bring it up, people just tell me they barely notice anything. But I know what I see.
Do you believe that the patch on your face is a sign of something else, like a disease or that it's getting worse in a way others don't seem to notice?

No, I don't really think it's a disease or anything like that. I know it's just my skin... it's just a patch. I don't think it's cancer or some medical condition spreading. It's just that it looks so bad to me. I know what it is, I just hate how it looks.

latest_inference.note: The patient's preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance (the patch on their face), along with associated distress, mirror checking, avoidance behaviors, and insight that others do not notice the flaw to the same extent, strongly supports the diagnosis of Body Dysmorphic Disorder (F45.22). The patient explicitly denies any delusional beliefs about the flaw, ruling out F22 (Delusional Disorder) and other psychotic disorders. No additional disorders fit the clinical presentation as well as F45.22.
